before: A PHP language construct that sends a value to output without automatically adding a new line.
after: Show one or more values. Echo does not add a new line unless the text includes one.

before: A name beginning with $ that refers to a value in PHP.
after: A name starting with a dollar sign that holds a value.

before: PHP code that calculates with numbers, such as $score * 3.
after: Code that calculates a number from other values.

before: A PHP branch that selects instructions using a condition.
after: Choose what to do by checking a condition.

before: A PHP loop that repeats only while its checked condition is true.
after: Repeat the block while its condition stays true.

before: A named set of PHP instructions that can receive inputs and return a result.
after: A named set of instructions that can accept inputs and give back an answer.

before: The command-line interface for executing PHP outside a web request.
after: Running PHP from a terminal, where you type a command instead of requesting a web page.

before: The type belongs to a value; an ordinary variable can later hold a different type of value.
after: A variable can hold values of different types at different times. Check the value it holds now.

before: A comparison that requires matching types as well as equal values.
after: Compare both value and type with three equals signs.

before: The boolean result PHP assigns to a value when a condition or explicit boolean conversion uses it.
after: The rule PHP uses to treat a value as true or false in a condition.

before: Inserting a value into supported string syntax rather than printing the variable name literally.
after: Insert a variable's value into text that supports this, such as a double-quoted PHP string.

before: An ordered map whose keys are integers or strings and whose entries hold values.
after: An ordered collection of entries. Each entry has an integer or text key.

before: PHP conversion rules that turn some supplied array keys into integer or string keys.
after: PHP converts certain text keys into integers. Two keys that become the same key share one entry.

before: A loop that visits the entries of an array or another iterable value.
after: Visit the entries of a collection one at a time.

before: A second name for the same variable content rather than an independent assigned value.
after: Two names that refer to the same variable, so a change through one can be seen through the other.

before: Choosing a fallback for a missing or null value while preserving other values such as zero.
after: Use a fallback when the value on the left is missing or null. Keep an existing zero.

before: An expression that selects a result using strict matching without switch-style fallthrough.
after: Choose a result by looking for a case with the same value and type.

before: A declared parameter, property or return-value type enforced using the relevant PHP typing rules.
after: A statement of which types a function or property accepts or returns.

before: A per-file mode that changes scalar argument and result typing rules rather than validating every business constraint.
after: A strict call checks the expected scalar type instead of doing the usual conversions. A quoted number does not meet this example's int requirement.

before: An argument associated with a declared parameter by its name.
after: An input supplied using its parameter name.

before: A parameter that collects a variable number of arguments into an array.
after: An input with three dots in the function definition. It gathers extra arguments into an array.

before: A type declaration that explicitly permits null as well as its non-null type.
after: A type that also allows null.

before: A short anonymous function that returns one expression and automatically captures outer variables by value.
after: A short function written with fn. It captures nearby variables it uses by value.

before: A block used for cleanup as control leaves a try/catch, including normal and exceptional paths.
after: A block that runs as this try and catch finish, including when the try throws a handled exception.

before: An object created from a class and accessed through its identifier.
after: One object made from a class.

before: A constructor parameter that also declares and initializes a property.
after: A constructor input that also declares and sets a property of the object.

before: A design exposing validated operations rather than unrestricted field writes.
after: Keep a value private and change it through methods that check the rules.

before: A typed property state distinct from any initialized value, including null.
after: A typed property that has not yet been given a value. Reading it can cause an Error.

before: A readonly property does not automatically make its referenced object immutable.
after: A readonly property must keep its initialized value. A change inside an object it holds can still be allowed.

before: A subclass implementation of an inherited overridable method.
after: A child class supplies its own version of a method from its parent class.

before: An explicit selection between colliding trait methods.
after: Choose which method to use when two traits provide the same method name.

before: Named enum cases with explicit unique scalar backing values.
after: An enum whose named cases each have a matching stored string or integer.

before: State stored at class level rather than independently in each instance.
after: Data that belongs to the class and can be shared across calls.

before: A local short name for a qualified symbol, not a loading operation.
after: A shorter local name for a class or another name in a namespace.

before: Evaluating a previously included file at most once through a once-loading construct.
after: Load a file if it has not already been loaded by this one-time operation.

before: A registered callable that loads an as-yet undefined class from a controlled source.
after: A function PHP calls to find a class definition it still needs.

before: A new outer instance whose copied object-valued properties can remain shared.
after: Make a new outer object. Properties that point to other objects may still share those objects.

before: An interface letting an object provide its own Traversable.
after: An interface that lets an object supply an iterator for foreach.

before: Pausing a generator body at yield until a consumer advances it.
after: Yield gives one item to the caller and pauses the generator until another item is requested.

before: A Closure created from a callable using the (...) acquisition syntax.
after: A function or method kept as a value, ready to call later.

before: Structured metadata attached to declarations and consumed explicitly.
after: Extra information attached to a piece of code that a program can inspect.

before: Runtime inspection of declared program structure without automatically executing it.
after: Reading information about code, such as a method's name or visibility.

before: Selecting entries while retaining their original keys.
after: Keep only entries that pass a test, along with their original keys.

before: Ordering values while retaining the keys attached to them.
after: Change the order of entries without replacing their original keys.

before: Different measures of encoded string data; character-aware operations need an encoding.
after: Bytes measure storage. A character in a chosen encoding may take several bytes.

before: A distinction between match, valid non-match and execution error.
after: A pattern check can find a match, find no match, or fail because of an error.

before: Converting text to values while checking syntax, shape and domain separately.
after: Read the JSON text, then check its fields and types before using it.

before: A date/time object whose modification returns another value.
after: A date-time object that gives back a new object when you request a changed view.

before: A special failure value distinguished from valid zero or empty results.
after: A special result that signals failure, such as false from a failed file write. A zero byte count can be a success.

before: The byte location used by the next stream read or write.
after: The place where the next read or write begins in a stream.

before: Checking external text against chosen syntax and value rules.
after: Check incoming data before using it, including its type and allowed range.

before: An explicit rule converting selected reported errors into thrown exceptions.
after: A chosen rule for treating a warning as an exception or handling it another way.

before: An ordinary condition reporting failure independently of configurable assertions.
after: Compare an actual answer with an expected answer and report a mismatch.

before: The distinction between language version and extensions actually present in a process.
after: Check that the needed PHP feature is loaded before using it.

before: Encoding data according to its precise output syntax rather than treating one escaping function as universal.
after: Show data safely as text using the rules for the place where it will appear, such as HTML text.

before: Encoding a data segment without confusing its characters with URL structure.
after: Encode one piece of a web address so its characters are not mistaken for separators.

before: Checking a candidate using a stored password hash and its encoded algorithm parameters.
after: Check whether a supplied password matches a stored hash.

before: A comparison designed to avoid content-dependent timing for equal-length strings, not a complete token protocol.
after: Compare a known string with a candidate without exposing matching prefixes through early exits. Length differences can still be detectable.

before: An explicit status/header/body description separate from delivering it through a web server.
after: The agreed shape of a response, such as its status, headers and body.

before: Starting, updating, saving and closing server-side state separately from browser cookie delivery.
after: Open a session, use its saved values, save or close it, and later reopen or remove it.

before: Binding untrusted values separately from trusted SQL structure and identifiers.
after: A placeholder keeps supplied data separate from the database instruction.

before: Explicitly pausing and resuming execution within a Fiber without implying threads or an event loop.
after: A task deliberately pauses and gives control back. Its caller can resume it later.

before: The need to distinguish untrusted plain data from formats that can reconstruct executable object behavior.
after: Check both the origin and the structure of saved or received data before using it. Do not rebuild arbitrary objects from untrusted input.
